v.why: Replacing a parameter-free skip on edge 0 with a conv gains much more (rows 3 and 6) than replacing a conv or none.
Replacing skip on edge 5 with a 3x3 conv gives the largest gains (row 53 and row 56) compared with replacing convs (rows 57 and 60).
Swapping pooling for a conv on the output edge gives a big gain in pool-heavy parents (rows 54 and 58).
Removing a 3x3 conv on edge 0 consistently hurts on all three datasets (rows 71, 75, 79 and 80).
Removing a skip on edge 0 helps or is neutral (rows 73 and 76), unlike removing a conv, which hurts.
Deleting the direct input-to-output 3x3 conv costs accuracy on all three datasets (rows 61 and 68), most of all on ImageNet16.
Replacing pooling on edge 4 with a 3x3 conv gives big gains in pool-heavy parents (row 44) and small positive gains elsewhere (row 47).
Replacing pooling on edge 2 with a 1x1 conv helps on all three datasets (rows 94 and 96), more than replacing a conv (rows 91 and 95).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 5 with pooling hurts on all datasets (rows 81, 85, 88 and 90).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 2 with a skip loses accuracy on all three datasets (rows 21 and 27).
